Hello! I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging that being a new mother can be a challenging and overwhelming experience, and it's completely normal to have a wide range of emotions during this time. I'm here to support you and provide a safe, non-judgmental space for you to express yourself.

As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns that may be affecting your well-being during the postpartum period. The purpose of this assessment is to get a better understanding of your emotional state and provide support and guidance if needed.

Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I'm here to listen and support you, not to judge. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us explore your feelings and experiences over the past 7 days. We'll take it one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation as comfortable and natural as possible.

So, let's get started. The first question is: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I still try to enjoy the little things, like when my baby smiles or does something cute, but it's just not the same as it was before. I feel like I've lost a bit of my sense of humor, and things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore. Some days are better than others, but overall, I'd say I've only really laughed a few times in the past week, and it's usually when my husband or family members are around and trying to make me feel better. When I'm alone with the baby, it's harder for me to find the funny side of things, and I often feel really overwhelmed and worried about everything.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I wish I could say the same. To be honest, it's been really tough for me to find the humor in things lately. Being a new mom is exhausting, and I feel like I'm just trying to survive most days. I'm constantly worried about my baby's health and safety, and it's hard for me to shake off those thoughts and just enjoy the moment. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and I've lost interest in a lot of things that used to bring me joy. Even when my baby does something cute or funny, I feel like I'm just pretending to laugh or smile, but deep down, I'm still feeling really anxious and overwhelmed. It's like I'm just trying to put on a brave face, but it's hard to genuinely feel happy or carefree when I'm feeling so tired and worried all the time.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

I haven't really been looking forward to things like I used to. I mean, I'll plan something, like a walk with my baby or a visit with friends, but when the time comes, I'll often feel anxious or overwhelmed, and I'll worry that I won't be able to get everything ready or that something will go wrong. It's hard for me to feel excited or enthusiastic about things when I'm feeling so tired and stressed out all the time. Even things that I used to enjoy, like reading or taking a bath, just feel like too much effort now. I'll think about doing something I used to like, but then I'll just feel guilty because I should be spending time with my baby or taking care of the house. It's like I've lost my sense of pleasure and enjoyment, and everything just feels like a chore. Sometimes I'll think about how I used to look forward to things, and it makes me feel sad and disappointed in myself, like I'm not the same person I used to be.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yes... that's something I've been doing a lot of lately. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something, whether it's because my baby is crying and I don't know how to soothe her, or because I didn't get the laundry done, or because I didn't make a healthy dinner. I'll think to myself, "I'm a terrible mother," or "I'm not doing enough," or "I'm not good enough." It's like I'm constantly criticizing myself and feeling guilty about everything. Even when my husband or family members try to reassure me that I'm doing a good job, I'll still feel like I'm failing somehow. It's hard for me to shake off those negative thoughts and feelings of inadequacy. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby or changing her diaper, and I'll start thinking about all the things I'm doing wrong and how I could be doing better. It's really hard for me to be kind to myself and give myself a break. I just feel like I'm not living up to my own expectations, and that's a really hard feeling to deal with.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

That's me, all the time. I worry about everything, and I mean everything. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, and I'll start thinking, "What if she's not getting enough milk?" or "What if she's not gaining enough weight?" or "What if I'm not doing this right?" And then my mind will just start racing, and I'll be worrying about all sorts of things that might happen, like her getting sick or hurt, or me not being able to take care of her. It's like my brain is constantly coming up with worst-case scenarios, and I have a hard time shutting them off. Sometimes I'll be lying in bed at night, and I'll be wide awake, thinking about all the things that could go wrong, and I'll feel my heart racing and my stomach churning. It's really scary, because I feel like I'm losing control, and I don't know how to make it stop. My husband will try to reassure me, and tell me that everything is okay, but it's hard for me to shake off those feelings of anxiety and worry. Even when there's no good reason to be worried, I'll still find something to worry about. It's like my mind is just wired to worry, and it's exhausting.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

Yes... that's happened to me a few times. I'll be sitting there, doing something normal, like changing my baby's diaper or feeding her, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. It's like my body is responding to some kind of threat, but there's no actual threat there. It's really scary, because I don't know what's happening or how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll be holding my baby, and I'll feel like I'm not safe, like something bad is going to happen to us. It's a really overwhelming feeling, and it's hard for me to calm down when it happens. I'll try to take deep breaths and remind myself that everything is okay, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of panic. It's like my body is on high alert all the time, waiting for something to go wrong. And it's not just when I'm alone with the baby, either - sometimes it happens when my husband is home, or when we're out with friends. It's like my anxiety is just lurking beneath the surface, waiting to pounce at any moment. It's really exhausting, and it's hard for me to feel like myself when I'm feeling so scared and panicky all the time.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes... that's a big understatement. Things have been completely overwhelming me, to be honest. I feel like I'm drowning in a sea of responsibility and exhaustion. Taking care of a new baby is hard, and it's not just the lack of sleep - it's the constant worry, the constant questioning of whether I'm doing everything right, the constant feeling of guilt when I'm not doing enough. And it's not just about the baby, either - it's about everything else, too. The house is a mess, I'm not cooking healthy meals, I'm not getting enough exercise... it's like I'm failing at everything, and it's all piling up on me. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and that if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just completely fall apart. I'll be sitting there, feeding my baby, and I'll start thinking about all the other things I need to do - laundry, dishes, grocery shopping - and I'll just feel this wave of overwhelm wash over me. It's like I'm trying to hold water in my hands, and it's just slipping through my fingers no matter how hard I try. I feel like I'm losing control, and it's really scary.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

That's me, every night. I'll be lying in bed, trying to fall asleep, but my mind is racing with all the things that are worrying me. I'll think about the baby, and whether she's okay, and whether I'm doing everything right. I'll think about all the things I need to do tomorrow, and how I'm going to get everything done. And I'll think about how I'm feeling, and how I just can't seem to shake off this sadness and anxiety. It's like my brain is a constant whirlwind of thoughts and worries, and it's impossible for me to calm down and relax. I'll try to focus on my breathing, or to distract myself with a book or something, but nothing seems to work. I'll toss and turn, feeling restless and anxious, and before I know it, hours have passed and I've only gotten a few minutes of sleep. And then, of course, the baby will wake up and need to be fed, and I'll be exhausted and irritable, and it's just this vicious cycle. Some nights are worse than others, but it's been really consistent lately - I'll get maybe 3 or 4 hours of sleep, and then I'll be up for the rest of the night, feeling miserable and overwhelmed. It's taking a toll on my physical health, too - I'm tired all the time, and I just feel like I'm running on empty.
I have felt sad or miserable

.. that's been me for a while now. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'll be taking care of the baby, and doing all the things I'm supposed to do, but inside, I'm just feeling so empty and sad. It's like I'm living in a fog, and I don't know how to get out of it. Sometimes I'll be holding my baby, and I'll start to feel this overwhelming sense of sadness, and I'll just start crying. It's like my emotions are just right there, on the surface, and I don't know how to control them. I'll be thinking about all the things that are stressing me out, like the baby's health, or our finances, or just the general overwhelm of being a new mom, and it's just too much for me to handle. I'll feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and then something will happen, and I'll just lose it. I'll cry, and I'll feel so guilty, because I'm supposed to be happy, right? I'm supposed to be enjoying this time with my new baby, but instead, I just feel sad and miserable. It's like I'm mourning the loss of my old life, or something. I don't know, it's just really hard for me to explain. I just feel like I'm not myself anymore, and it's really scary.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like the smallest thing will set me off, and I'll just start sobbing. I'll be changing the baby's diaper, or feeding her, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll start crying. Sometimes it's because I'm feeling overwhelmed, and sometimes it's because I'm just feeling so sad and alone. I'll cry because I'm tired, or because I'm feeling guilty about something, or just because I'm feeling like I'm not doing enough. It's like my emotions are just right there, on the surface, and I don't know how to control them. I'll try to hold it in, but sometimes it's just too much, and I'll break down. My husband will try to comfort me, and he'll tell me that everything is okay, but it's hard for me to believe him when I'm feeling so overwhelmed. I'll feel like I'm a burden to him, and that he's just trying to be nice, but he doesn't really understand what I'm going through. The crying is just so exhausting, too. It's like my body is just drained, and I don't have the energy to do anything else. I'll cry, and then I'll feel guilty for crying, because I'm supposed to be strong, and I'm supposed to be able to handle this. But the truth is, I don't feel strong. I feel weak, and vulnerable, and just really, really sad.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

No... I don't think about harming myself. I mean, I feel really overwhelmed and sad, and I don't know how to make it stop, but I don't think about hurting myself. I think about how I just want to feel better, and how I want to be a good mom to my baby. I think about how I want to get through this difficult time, and how I want to find a way to be happy again. Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding on, but I don't think about hurting myself. I think about how I need to keep going, for my baby's sake, and for my own sake. I just want to get through this, and find a way to feel like myself again.
